answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by bonding real stake to identity: every agent locks collateral before its vote counts, and random juries audit behavior each round. A thousand fake voices then need a thousand bonds, so the attacker pays roughly linearly in capital, while slashed stakes reward the honest jurors who catch vote-copying. That bond is the crystal making identity costly, the rotating jury a garden where trust can grow, and the forfeited collateral as immovable as basalt, turning identity flooding into a losing business.
